name: Editing Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing editing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing editing style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing editing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing editing style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any editing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Prefer explicit, readable editing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. When editing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Keep editing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Keep editing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Validate editing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. When multiple editing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen editing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Check that editing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic editing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop editing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting editing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about editing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
